passages.quote:
This guidance was last updated in October 2018.

Statement of compliance with the Pre-release Access to Official Statistics Order 2008

The Department for Education’s (DfE’s) statement of compliance with the Pre-release Access to Official Statistics Order 2008 sets out DfE’s operational arrangements for giving ministers and officials pre-release access to official statistics 24 hours prior to publication.

The Order tightens the rules and principles governing pre-release access to official statistics prior to publication.

The scope of the Order extends to all official statistics produced by DfE and its public bodies.

National Statistician’s guidance on identifying official statistics identifies 5 criteria when considering if information should be considered as official statistics:

the data collection on which the statistics are based should be conducted on a regular basis

results should be compiled using widely accepted statistical methods

coverage should be representative of the whole population in question

the subject matter has the potential to inform, or impact on, decisions about the management of government services, or the allocation of public funds or resources

the information is placed in the public domain

National statistics are a subset of official statistics that have been assessed and comply with or are deemed to have been assessed and comply with the Code of Practice for Statistics. The decision on whether information is classified as official statistics is made on a case-by-case basis by the Head of Profession for Statistics.

The Pre-release Access to Official Statistics Order 2008 commenced on 1 December 2008.

Contact DfE

Direct any queries to:

Telephone: 020 7783 8300

By email: hop.statistics@education.gov.uk.

Introduction

This statement sets out DfE’s operational arrangements for giving ministers and officials pre-release access to official statistics in their final form 24 hours prior to publication.

These arrangements are designed to ensure that such access is justified, limited, controlled and publicised and complies with statutory requirements. The purpose of these arrangements and their transparency via this statement is to maintain public confidence in the integrity of official statistics while allowing ministers to make a public response or take action at or shortly after the time of publication where those statistics cover policy or operational areas for which they are democratically responsible.

Exclusion

Different arrangements apply to pre-release access to DfE’s own management or administrative data where these data subsequently form the basis for published official statistics.

Authority

These arrangements have been drawn up by DfE’s Head of Profession for Statistics in consultation with the Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR). The Head of Profession for Statistics is also responsible for ensuring the day-to-day implementation of these arrangements.

Organisations should appoint a head of profession for statistics (HoP) where an official body:

produces national statistics

produces an appreciable number of official statistics

produces particularly high-profile official statistics

employs an appreciable number of statisticians

HoPs should be appointed by departments in consultation with the Office of the National Statistician. The core of the role of an HoP is a responsibility to ensure that their organisation complies with:

the Code of Practice for Statistics

pre-release access orders

relevant data-related legislation

the National Statistician’s guidance on management information

General principle

DfE operates under the rules and principles set out in the Pre-release Access to Official Statistics Order 2008, which states that pre-release access to official statistics must be:

allowed only in circumstances where the public benefit likely to result from such access outweighs the detriment to public trust in official statistics likely to result from doing so

limited to the minimum number of persons deemed necessary to allow the minister to either:

i. respond to questions, or make statements about the statistics at, or shortly after, the time of publication of those statistics, or

ii. take action before, at the time of, or shortly after the publication of those statistics

Grant of pre-release access

Pre-release access will be limited to those persons who meet the eligibility criteria set out in Annex A(i) for purposes that meet the criteria in General principle. Recipients may share their access with their administrative support staff even though those staff may not directly engage with the statistics in question.

Pre-release access will only apply to official statistics in their final form that meet the eligibility criteria set out in Annex A(ii). Special circumstances covers special circumstances where official statistics may be shared more than 24 hours prior to publication.

Pre-release access as set out in this statement does not apply to access to official statistics by those persons:

engaged in the process of producing and disseminating the statistics in question (including those responsible for overseeing this process)

requested by the producers to quality assure the statistics before their public release

Documentation and publication

In the interests of openness and transparency, DfE maintains a public record in Annex B listing the titles of all the statistical releases to which these arrangements apply.

A list of those who have been granted pre-release access as well as the job titles and the organisations to which they belong are published alongside each official statistics publication to which pre-release access has been granted. The justification for giving advance access to each listed recipient is available on request.
